title: FuXi-Linear: Unleashing the Power of Linear Attention in Long-term Time-aware Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Quadratic-complexity attention limits the handling of long user sequences and slows inference.

gap.claim: Existing linear-attention recommendation research inadequately handles temporal signals, positional information, long sequences, and deep architectures.

contributions.claim: FuXi-Linear is a linear-complexity model for efficient long-sequence recommendation.

The model uses a Temporal Retention Channel for independently computing periodic temporal attention weights and a Linear Positional Channel for integrating positional information with learnable kernels.
FuXi-Linear exhibits scaling properties at a thousand-length sequence scale.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On sequences of several thousand tokens, FuXi-Linear reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art models in recommendation quality.
Compared with competitive baselines, the model reportedly achieves up to 10× speedup in prefill and up to 21× speedup in decode.
The authors report that the code is publicly released.

narrative_sequence.summary: Quadratic attention limits long-sequence recommendation and inference efficiency.
Existing linear-attention approaches have shortcomings in temporal modeling, positional information, and long or deep sequence processing.
The paper proposes FuXi-Linear with temporal-retention and linear-positional channels.
The authors report thousand-length scaling behavior and evaluation on sequences of several thousand tokens.
The authors report quality improvements, decoding and prefill speedups, and public code release.

source_observation.claim: Separating temporal processing from semantic processing is reported to prevent crosstalk between the two signal types.

interpretation.claim: When different signal types can interfere, explicitly decoupling their computation may improve controllability.

application.claim: Consider separate processing channels for temporal and semantic information in long-sequence recommendation systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation benefits other domains or signal combinations.

source_observation.claim: The reported evaluation uses sequences of several thousand tokens and reports stage-specific speedups.

interpretation.claim: Long-context system evaluations should distinguish computational stages because performance gains may differ between prefill and decode.

application.claim: Report separate prefill and decode measurements when evaluating long-sequence recommendation inference.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the hardware, workloads, metrics, or experimental settings needed to generalize the reported speedups.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, and baseline identities are unspecified.
Architectural depth, training setup, hardware, and runtime measurement procedures are unspecified.
The scope and details of the reported scaling behavior are unspecified.
